verdicts.note: Control-arm bracket detaching from a rusted crossmember could be read as STRUCTURE, but the complainant frames it as the suspension mounting point and all models agreed.
Rambling letter about the car being repossessed; names no vehicle system at all.
Vehicle burned down with no cause identified -- correctly NOT routed to a causal system, per the fire gotcha.

REVISES THE PRIOR ADJUDICATION, which keyed on the AdvanceTrac/hill-descent warning lights and missed that the dealer diagnosed the RESTRAINT CONTROL MODULE -- an airbag-system component (which on Ford also feeds yaw data to AdvanceTrac). gpt-5-mini's AIR BAGS answer is well supported, so both labels are accepted.
Vacuum brake-assist loss and unintended driveline braking, with no air/electric evidence either way -- all three brake subtypes are claimed by their own definitions.

BORDERLINE: complainant attributes it to 'an electrical short in the stalk', but only the headlights are affected and the EXTERIOR LIGHTING definition applies when the lighting itself is the stated problem.

Five distinct problems. The complainant's own stated main concern is that the car shuts off and the steering locks, so gpt-5.4-mini's STEERING is at least as defensible as the two labels already accepted.
'Cooling line' here carries transmission fluid, so POWER TRAIN rather than engine cooling.
All three models said TIRES. The narrative is mostly about repeated flats and a blowout, but Goodyear diagnosed rim issues, which is what WHEELS covers. Both readings are supported by the text.

TENSION WITH 471641: paint peeling there was accepted as UNKNOWN OR OTHER, while paint delaminating here is STRUCTURE. Defensible because this one names a specific body component (windshield pillar) and that one led with paint plus A/C plus locks, but the two rows do pull in different directions.

Confirmed via raw data: PROD_TYPE for this row is a standalone child-safety-seat product, not PROD_TYPE='V' (vehicle) -- gotcha B8 already says the project should be scoped to PROD_TYPE='V' to avoid exactly this. Remove from the dataset entirely rather than force a vehicle-system label onto a non-vehicle product complaint. User confirmed deletion 2026-08-31.
